traits.question_notes: 3 year old with "very large" emotions. Parents were big on physical resolution of issues (had an older brother). Sit down with him, talk to him, ask him about how he is feeling. Each child is different. Emotions are teachable moments.
Felt like the director was not running things as she should because director did not have the support that she needed. Expressed how she felt. Take a small break, breathe, reset.
No is a big word in the toddler phase. "My biggest concern is always safety." if the kids run, don't chase them. ask for help from co-teacher.

earlier in career, (in her 20's) she was on her phone in the class. Learned if they say no phone, then no phones. Anopther school had a very strict curriculumn. Once you divert your attention to a phone, you are not supervising.

there have been a lot of times she had activities planned, and the kids were not interested. Lead by what they like, but still try to introduce them to something different. If kids are not interested, still try to start the activity and see if they get interested. Integrate things they are interested into the lesson. Try again at another time.
we are all human being, make mistakes, and always learning. Likes to do social media content creation. Have to pay attention to developmental stages, home life, and the whole picture.
pay attention to cues. they have different cries. you have to have an interest in figuring it out."
